repo.description: A high-throughput and memory-efficient inference and serving engine for LLMs
repo.name: vllm

detail.body:
## Overview

Add two Zen CPU hardware-test steps (kernel + platform-detection) on the `zen5`
queue, gated on zen source changes. They reuse the zen CPU image published by the
existing `zen-cpu-image-build` step instead of recompiling on the scarce Zen5 box:
that step now **pushes** `<repo>:<commit>-zen-cpu` to public ECR, and
`run-zen-cpu-test.sh` **pulls** it (with a local-build fallback). Builds on the
merged zen image-build work in #60016; assumes the zentorch 2.14.0.1 / fp16
enablement from #61411.

## Claims

- Adds `Zen-CPU-Kernel Tests` and `Zen-CPU-Platform-Detection Tests` on
  `device: zen5`, gated on zen source changes.
- `zen-cpu-image-build` now publishes `<repo>:<commit>-zen-cpu` to public ECR, so
  the zen5 steps pull it (anonymous pull, no credentials on the test side) rather
  than rebuilding on scarce hardware.
- `run-zen-cpu-test.sh` pulls the prebuilt zen image (local-build fallback:
  published `-cpu` base, else from source); installs zentorch directly via
  `ZENTORCH_VERSION` to avoid the `vllm[zen]` transitive triton-cpu URL failure;
  verifies the installed zentorch version + its `torch.compile` backend before
  tests; and removes pulled/built images on exit so they don't accumulate on the
  shared host.
- Adds a consistency test asserting the `ZENTORCH_VERSION` in `cpu.yaml` and
  `run-zen-cpu-test.sh` match the `zen` extra in `setup.py`.
- Gates the fp16 case of `test_cpu_unquantized_gemm_dispatch.py` on
  `zentorch_is_fp16_supported()` (AVX512-FP16 / Venice+), so the Turin-class zen5
  CI doesn't run an fp16 matmul the hardware can't execute.

## Validation

**Full flow verified end-to-end in CI (build #98237)**, commit `22762f66…`:
- `image-build-cpu` pushes `…:<commit>-cpu`.
- `zen-cpu-image-build` logs `Using published CPU image as base: …-cpu`,
  installs `zentorch==2.14.0.1` (no `vllm[zen]`, no triton error),
  `Login Succeeded`, pushes `…-zen-cpu`.
- Both zen5 steps log `Using published Zen image: …-zen-cpu` — reuse confirmed,
  not the fallback.
- Kernel step: `7 passed, 1 skipped` (fp16 skipped on this non-AVX512-FP16
  part); Platform step: `10 passed`.

## Details

- Reuse mirrors the existing `-cpu` image reuse: the push is guarded on `REGISTRY`
  (CI only); pulls are anonymous public ECR, so test nodes need no credentials.
  The zen5 agent env lacks `REGISTRY`/`REPO`, so the test steps pass the
  public-ECR coordinates explicitly (matching `ci_config.yaml`'s main/premerge
  mapping).
- Test steps `depends_on: zen-cpu-image-build` with `allow_dependency_failure:
  true`, so the local-build fallback still runs if that build fails/soft-fails.
  `run-zen-cpu-test.sh` is in the build step's `source_file_dependencies` so the
  build step is never pruned while a test runs (which would otherwise make
  `depends_on` error at pipeline upload).
- `ZENTORCH_VERSION` pinned to `2.14.0.1` (matching the `zen` extra in `setup.py`,
  per #61411) keeps `Dockerfile.zen` on its direct-zentorch `if` branch and avoids
  `uv` re-resolving `vllm[zen]` (which fails on vLLM's transitive `triton @ <url>`
  CPU wheel).
- The zen5 preflight asserts `importlib.metadata.version("zentorch")` equals the
  pin and `"zentorch" in torch._dynamo.list_backends()`, so a version/ABI mismatch
  or a stable-only build fails loudly instead of silently testing a different
  zentorch.
- fp16: the dispatch test's fp16 parametrize is skipped when
  `zentorch_is_fp16_supported()` is false; the mock-zentorch x86 lane (no such op)
  still exercises fp16 via its `F.linear` stub, mirroring
  `ZenCpuPlatform.supported_dtypes`.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** CI/test-only; reuses the existing published-image pattern, adds no runtime core-component code, and isolates the push behind a registry guard with a local-build fallback.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** This PR is the test wiring; the full build→push→pull→test flow is verified end-to-end in CI build #98237 and reproduced locally. fp16 is gated to hardware that supports it.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Additive, no unrelated formatting; comments describe the current pull/fallback/credential design (stale CPU-reuse comments corrected).
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Summary, concrete claims, end-to-end validation evidence, and implementation trade-offs included.
</details>

+#!/bin/bash
+
+# Run the AMD Zen CPU tests on the zen5 hardware.
+
+set -euox pipefail
+
+# allow to bind to different cores
+CORE_RANGE=${CORE_RANGE:-0-47}
+NUMA_NODE=${NUMA_NODE:-0}
+IMAGE_NAME="zen-cpu-test-$NUMA_NODE"
+FALLBACK_BASE_IMAGE="zen-cpu-base-$NUMA_NODE"
+TIMEOUT_VAL=$1
+TEST_COMMAND=$2
+
+# Install zentorch directly in Dockerfile.zen instead of `uv pip install
+# "vllm[zen]"`, which makes uv re-resolve vLLM and fail on its transitive
+# triton-cpu URL dependency. Keep in sync with the `zen` extra in setup.py.
+ZENTORCH_VERSION="${ZENTORCH_VERSION:-2.14.0.1}"
+
+CLEANUP_IMAGES=()
+cleanup() {
+    if [ "${#CLEANUP_IMAGES[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
+        docker rmi -f "${CLEANUP_IMAGES[@]}" > /dev/null 2>&1 || true
+    fi
+}
+trap cleanup EXIT
+
+# Published images (resolvable only when the Buildkite registry env vars are
+# present, i.e. in CI). Pulls from public ECR are anonymous.
+ZEN_IMAGE=""
+SHARED_CPU_IMAGE=""
+if [ -n "${REGISTRY:-}" ] && [ -n "${REPO:-}" ] && [ -n "${BUILDKITE_COMMIT:-}" ]; then
+    ZEN_IMAGE="$REGISTRY/$REPO:$BUILDKITE_COMMIT-zen-cpu"
+    SHARED_CPU_IMAGE="$REGISTRY/$REPO:$BUILDKITE_COMMIT-cpu"
+fi
+
+if [ -n "$ZEN_IMAGE" ] && docker pull "$ZEN_IMAGE"; then
+    # Fast path: reuse the prebuilt zen image; no local build.
+    echo "--- :docker: Using published Zen image: $ZEN_IMAGE"
+    IMAGE_NAME="$ZEN_IMAGE"
+    CLEANUP_IMAGES+=("$ZEN_IMAGE")
+else
+    # Step 1: obtain the CPU base image that Dockerfile.zen layers on. Prefer
+    # pulling the published `-cpu` image; fall back to building it from source.
+    if [ -n "$SHARED_CPU_IMAGE" ] && docker pull "$SHARED_CPU_IMAGE"; then
+        echo "--- :docker: Using published CPU image as base: $SHARED_CPU_IMAGE"
+        BASE_IMAGE="$SHARED_CPU_IMAGE"
+        CLEANUP_IMAGES+=("$SHARED_CPU_IMAGE")
+    else
+        echo "--- :docker: Published CPU image unavailable; building base from source"
+        docker build --progress plain --tag "$FALLBACK_BASE_IMAGE" \
+            --target vllm-openai -f docker/Dockerfile.cpu .
+        BASE_IMAGE="$FALLBACK_BASE_IMAGE"
+        CLEANUP_IMAGES+=("$FALLBACK_BASE_IMAGE")
+    fi
+
+    # Step 2: build the zen test image on top of the CPU base.
+    echo "--- :docker: Building Zen test image"
+    docker build --progress plain --tag "$IMAGE_NAME" \
+        --build-arg BASE_IMAGE="$BASE_IMAGE" \
+        --build-arg ZENTORCH_VERSION="$ZENTORCH_VERSION" \
+        --target vllm-zen-test -f docker/Dockerfile.zen .
+    CLEANUP_IMAGES+=("$IMAGE_NAME")
+fi
+
+# Run the image, setting --shm-size=4g for tensor parallel. The in-container
+# command verifies the installed zentorch matches the pinned version and that
+# its torch.compile backend is registered (i.e. not the stable-only build), so
+# a mismatch fails loudly instead of silently testing a different zentorch.
+docker run --rm \
+    --cpuset-cpus="$CORE_RANGE" \
+    --cpuset-mems="$NUMA_NODE" \
+    -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \
+    --privileged=true \
+    -e HF_TOKEN \
+    -e VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=16 \
+    -e VLLM_CPU_CI_ENV=1 \
+    -e VLLM_CPU_SIM_MULTI_NUMA=1 \
+    --shm-size=4g \
+    "$IMAGE_NAME" \
+    timeout "$TIMEOUT_VAL" bash -c "set -euox pipefail
+echo \"--- Print packages\"
+pip list
+echo \"--- Verify zentorch\"
+python -c \"
+import importlib.metadata as m, torch, zentorch
+from torch._dynamo import list_backends
+v = m.version('zentorch')
+assert v == '${ZENTORCH_VERSION}', (
+    'zentorch ' + v + ' != expected ${ZENTORCH_VERSION}'
+)
+assert 'zentorch' in list_backends(), (
+    'zentorch torch.compile backend not registered (stable-only build?)'
+)
+\"
+echo \"--- Running tests\"
+${TEST_COMMAND}"

 # authoritative source for the torch version it must track.
 CPU_REQUIREMENTS = REPO_ROOT / "requirements" / "cpu.txt"
+# The zen CI image build and the zen5 local-build fallback each carry their own
+# copy of the zentorch pin; they must match setup.py so CI installs the same
+# zentorch that `vllm[zen]` would.
+CPU_PIPELINE = REPO_ROOT / ".buildkite" / "hardware_tests" / "cpu.yaml"
+ZEN_TEST_SCRIPT = (
+    REPO_ROOT / ".buildkite" / "scripts" / "hardware_ci" / "run-zen-cpu-test.sh"
+)

@@ -77,3 +84,46 @@ def test_zentorch_pin_tracks_torch_release():
         f"torch=={torch_version}. When bumping torch, bump the first three "
         "components of the zentorch pin in setup.py to match."
     )
+
+
+def _extract_ci_zentorch_pins() -> dict[str, str]:
+    """Pull the ZENTORCH_VERSION the zen CI build/test paths hardcode."""
+    pins: dict[str, str] = {}
+
+    # cpu.yaml: `ZENTORCH_VERSION: "2.x.x.x"` in the zen-cpu-image-build step.
+    yaml_matches = re.findall(
+        r"(?m)^\s*ZENTORCH_VERSION:\s*[\"']?([0-9][0-9A-Za-z.\-+]*)",
+        CPU_PIPELINE.read_text(),
+    )
+    assert yaml_matches, f"No 'ZENTORCH_VERSION:' pin found in {CPU_PIPELINE}"
+    assert len(set(yaml_matches)) == 1, (
+        f"Conflicting ZENTORCH_VERSION pins in {CPU_PIPELINE}: {yaml_matches}"
+    )
+    pins[str(CPU_PIPELINE)] = yaml_matches[0]
+
+    # run-zen-cpu-test.sh: `ZENTORCH_VERSION="${ZENTORCH_VERSION:-2.x.x.x}"`.
+    sh_matches = re.findall(
+        r"ZENTORCH_VERSION:-([0-9][0-9A-Za-z.\-+]*)",
+        ZEN_TEST_SCRIPT.read_text(),
+    )
+    assert sh_matches, (
+        f"No 'ZENTORCH_VERSION:-<version>' default found in {ZEN_TEST_SCRIPT}"
+    )
+    assert len(set(sh_matches)) == 1, (
+        f"Conflicting ZENTORCH_VERSION defaults in {ZEN_TEST_SCRIPT}: {sh_matches}"
+    )
+    pins[str(ZEN_TEST_SCRIPT)] = sh_matches[0]
+
+    return pins
+
+
+def test_ci_zentorch_pins_match_setup():
+    expected = _extract_zentorch_version()
+
+    for path, version in _extract_ci_zentorch_pins().items():
+        assert version == expected, (
+            f"{path} pins ZENTORCH_VERSION={version} but setup.py pins "
+            f"zentorch=={expected}. These must stay in sync so the zen CI image "
+            "build and the zen5 local-build fallback install the same zentorch "
+            "that `vllm[zen]` resolves; update them together."
+        )

inline_comments.body: setup.py:1714 has pinned zentorch==2.14.0.1 since #61411, which is already in this PR's base, and the zen build step uses 2.14.0.1 too (cpu.yaml:281). Whenever the zen image pull fails, the local build here installs zentorch 2.13.0.1 on the torch 2.14.0 base. Its import then warns about the mismatch and loads only libzentorch_stable.so: no compile backend and no zentorch_sdpa op. So the zen5 job tests a different zentorch than users get, depending on whether the pull worked, and the two current tests still pass because they mock around it.

- `/amd-ci retry` retries failed jobs in AMD CI for the current PR head. Use `/amd-ci run` when the current head has no AMD CI build.
